title: Onboarding to DevOps Team
content:
This page is internal and created for new team members that joins the IPEX DevOps Team.

Who we Are

We’re currently three members in our team who work with the following objectives:

  • Strategic imperatives

    • OKRs, such as those outlined here

  • Proactive and reactive support, for example:

    • Onboarding and migrating teams and products to GitHub

    • Various tools and platform support, and the access- and access levels to those tools

Before diving further into our space it is important to first be well acquainted with the generic onboarding and offboarding principles.

Security Mindset

As we in the team are involved with DevOps and DevSecOps, and recommend, guide, and promote security work, it’s important that you embrace and follow the IPEX Security general guidelines and recommendations.

Work Methodology

We have daily standup meetings, which we rather refer to as sync meetings, in which we both plan our work and talk about certain issues or questions that have arisen recently. These meetings start at 09:30 CET as of this writing, and usually last for about 30 minutes.

On Thursdays these sync meetings differ a bit since , who is development manager, also attends. In these meetings we report and discuss progress on our mid- and long-term objectives.

Jira Board

Our daily sync meetings revolve around our Jira board, currently categorized as:

  • Support

    • Mostly reactive support to teams and colleagues currently experiencing issues or problems

  • Improve

  • Migrating teams and products to GitHub

  • Software development process

  • Application monitoring

    • For example, tools like New Relic and Sentry

  • IPEX Tech Radar (more about that

  • DORA Metrics

    • Part of the current OKRs, more information about it here

Onboarding Teams

As part of migrating products from e.g. Bitbucket to GitHub we use to setup meetings with the following stakeholders in the teams:

  • Product Owner

  • Solution Architect / Technical Lead

  • DevOps representative (if present)

In the meeting we clarify our process; our roles and what our current solutions are. We discuss the current solution, potential problems and/or risks with the current solutions and how they can be mitigated.

The meetings resemble an architecture forum in which we discus pros and cons, low effort vs high value, etc.

Once settled we initiate work such as:

  • Creating Azure subscriptions and service principals

  • IaC - Infrastructure as Code and Terraform: Introductions, knowledge sharing and discussion

  • Initiating the GitHub Actions workflows and their design

  • Prototyping and POCs

  • Testing pipelines

Meetings and Associates

We work closely with the following teams:

  • Communication and Ways of Working

    • Main driver for the ways of working part is Wiveka Göransson

  • Quality

    • Main driver for this area is

The following regular meetings are held with these teams:

  • DevOps Initiative

Other regular meetings with other teams and stakeholders are:

  • DevOps Community

  • IPEX Steering

    • Occurs once a month

    • Reporting on progress to upper management

  • IPEX Architecture and Development Meetings

    • Discussions around architectural roadmaps, decisions, and current issues

Meeting Guidelines

It may a bit stressful or difficult to prioritize meetings with your work duties. There are some general guidelines here, and internally we have the following guidelines:

  • DevOps Initiative: We decide how many of us will attend this meeting on a week by week basis. Seldom everybody needs to attend these meetings.

We should strive not to include all members in all internal meetings. The decision needs to be based on the topic. For example, if two DevOps engineers have developed two different parts of a solution, and there needs to be a decision on way forward, then all team members may be needed. For help with issues, troubleshooting, getting stuck, reach out to the teammate who you think is most appropriate to help you with the issue.

The bottom line is that you should try to find an efficient balance between the meetings and your tasks, so this section is only some general guidelines.

Furthermore, always include a distinct agenda for each meeting you call for.

Tools and Technologies

Many of our tools and technologies use MFA (Multi Factor Authentication), so that area would be one of the first to address. Follow this guide to learn more about Auth0 and MFA Defender. And also install the appropriate software on your phone, for example Google Authenticator, if not already done.

Also read through Account Management to get an overview and understanding of our cloud vendors and choices.

Communication Tools

The basis for all communication is MS Teams and Slack. For teams you should already have been granted access to some channels. The teams channels that involve DevOps are:

  • DevOps Initiative (on behalf of IPEX Ways of Working)

  • IPEX DevOps

  • IPEX DevOps Community

  • DevOps Platform

In Slack the channels related to DevOps and our current work are:

  • # ipex-devops-team

    • Our internal team channel

  • # ipex-devops

    • The IPEX DevOps channel

As practice we’ve started to create dedicated Slack channels for the migrations to GitHub. Examples are:

  • # storageone-github-migration

    • Discussions around the migration and support for the Storage One team

  • # storagetwo-github-migration

    • Discussions around the migration and support for the Storage Two team

These channels may be temporary, but could potentially last for a while since there may be continuous support even after the migrations are done.

GitHub

Whether you already have an active GitHub account or if you want to create a new account we have compiled this guide to get you onboarded to GitHub. As part of the DevOps team you have full access to all teams' repositories. Much of our work consist of helping other teams, or developing GitHub Actions and/or reusable workflows, which we then support from a software maintenance perspective. Previously much of our work constituted migrating from Bitbucket Pipelines to GitHub. In our team we have one POC/sandbox repository, in which you can get started trying out things.

Keeping Updated with GitHub News

We’re continuously trying to keep updated on GitHub news and roadmaps, and we subscribe (via devops@inter.ikea.com), to https://resources.github.com/newsletter/.

Azure

As part of your onboarding you should also have access to Azure and Azure Portal. As Azure offers a wide range of features and technologies, some of the most important at IPEX are:

  • Azure Artifacts

    • This is the current recommended way for storing artifacts and artifact dependencies

    • We help other teams setting up and connecting to their feeds

    • We’re currently working on removing direct dependencies towards npmjs

  • Azure AD

  • Azure subscriptions, roles, and privileges

    • Note: Subscriptions are managed and created by Joakim Hogart in our team

  • Azure Functions

  • Azure DevOps

    • While teams are allowed to run pipelines in Azure DevOps our recommendation is to use GitHub Actions

    • Release pipelines are currently not used at IPEX

    • All repositories are hosted on GitHub

  • Service Principals

    • You will most likely be part in ordering service principals for teams.

AWS

AWS, currently, is not the platform suggested by IPEX, but since there are many planners and products currently hosted on AWS (some which may never leave AWS) it is important to be acquainted with the fundamentals. We also generate API keys in AWS for deployment metrics, so this guide will help you out once API keys are requested by the teams.

Akamai

IPEX uses Akamai and Akamai NetStorage to host the planners. It is thus important to familiarize yourself with this platform. Some other links to read are:

  • Akamai Support

  • AoA Akamai Setup

  • Rclone

Terraform

We strongly believe in Iac (Infrastructure as Code) and use Terraform to maintain and setup resources.

Confluence

We use confluence as our documentation platform, which you should already have access to during your onboarding. Feel free to update pages at any time - this requires no permission or pre-approval. The IPEX home landing page can be found here.

For questions and access requests to our tools please contact Joakim Hogart.
